result.judge_notes: pass 1 (A=with, B=without): A says the stylesheet is already sound, names what works (size, measure, leading, h2 spacing, kicker), and keeps nearly every value. Its main stated reason is wrong, though: browsers already make h1 and h2 bold by default, so adding font-weight: 700 changes nothing. B is close to a rewrite that changes colors, enlarges the headings and blockquote, adds a drop cap, suggests swapping the typeface, and slightly tightens the line height. | pass 2 (A=without, B=with): B says plainly that most of the sheet is already sound, names the size, measure, leading, h2 spacing and kicker as things that work, keeps nearly every value, and gives a reason with values for each small change. Its claim that regular-weight headings cause the plain look is wrong, though: h1 and h2 are bold by default, so setting font-weight: 700 does nothing. A rewrites most values, changes colors, adds a drop cap and a heavier pull quote, recommends a new typeface, and tightens the body line-height to 1.6 while enlarging the body size and headings.
